power.title: Power Analysis Check
report: No power analyses were detected.

::: {.callout-tip title="Learn More" collapse="true"}

Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size.

For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like:

> An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen's d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group.

For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like:

> A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5.

:::

text.text: Psychometric network analysis faces a foundational methodological divide: while rejecting the latent common-cause assumption, applied studies evaluate composite score reliability using classical common-cause coefficients (α, ω) or substitute metric precision with bootstrap partition frequencies (bootEGA), incurring indirect reliability induction under REGEMA guidelines and violating AERA/APA/NCME testing standards.

We introduce Reliability Exploratory Graph Analysis (rEGA), an analytical framework grounded in supportconstrained maximum likelihood refitting (𝐊 ̂refit ) and the Neumann-Markov resolvent operator (𝐐 = [𝐈 -𝛀] -1 ). rEGA establishes the Law of Conservation of the Nodal Triad, partitioning standardized item variance into Within-Community Communality (ℎ 𝑖 2 ), Inter-Community Bridging Variance (𝛽 𝑖 2 ), and Markov Nodal Uniqueness (𝜓 𝑖 2 ), such that ℎ 𝑖 2 + 𝛽 𝑖 2 + 𝜓 𝑖 2 ≡ 1.000.

From this decomposition, rEGA defines a purity-weighted adjacency matrix (𝐀 rEGA ), Within-Community (Γ 𝑐 ) and Total Network (Γ 𝑡 ) reliability coefficients, and the Graph Standard Error of Measurement (SEM raw ).
Across a Monte Carlo simulation of 97,200 datasets (972 conditions), rEGA-Leiden outperformed Walktrap, Louvain, and Parallel Analysis in dimensionality recovery (87.65% vs.

64.81%-71.32%), eliminated ℓ 1 -shrinkage bias (RMSE 𝜓 = .035), classified core, bridge, and noise nodes with 86.8%-99.4% accuracy, and yielded unbiased reliability estimates (Bias Γ = -.007) immune to lexical doublet inflation.

Multi-sample validation on the AAQ-II (𝑁 = 3,200) and DASS-21 (𝑁 = 2,751) demonstrated that the Nodal Triad Leakage Criterion (𝛽 ̅ 2 > ℎ ̅ 2 ) rules out spurious over-fragmentation while distinguishing noisy items (A1) from transdiagnostic bridges (D2, S3, S6) with high cross-sample invariance (𝑟 > .93).

text.text: Separating structural validity from score error, rEGA prevents ad hoc scale pruning and reconciles network psychometrics with international measurement standards.

text.text: To address these methodological limitations, the present study formalizes and empirically validates Reliability Exploratory Graph Analysis (rEGA), an extension of the network framework designed to integrate measurement error decomposition and metric reliability estimation into the assessment of internal structure.

Three specific objectives are proposed: (1) To evaluate, via a large-scale Monte Carlo simulation study, the accuracy of rEGA in recovering dimensional structure, estimating the conditional precision matrix, and quantifying metric reliability across varying conditions of sample size, factor loading magnitude, and noise contamination; (2) to examine the diagnostic utility of rEGA on the Acceptance and Action Questionnaire (AAQ-II) across multiple independent samples, testing whether the dimensional over-fragmentation identified by traditional EGA stems from lexical redundancy among items and evaluating its repercussions on composite score reliability; (3) to investigate the performance of rEGA on the Depression, Anxiety, and Stress Scales (DASS-21) in community and psychiatric clinical populations, assessing the recovery of its theoretical dimensions, the differentiation between indicators affected by conditional error versus transdiagnostic connectors, and the invariance of the nodal profile across samples.

The Reliability Exploratory Graph Analysis (rEGA) model unfolds across six sequential algebraic stages that transform the observed covariance matrix into a network representation purified of conditional error, enabling closed-form estimation of metric reliability and exact decomposition of nodal variance.

The operational formulation of each stage is presented below in the main text; for complete analytical proofs, non-negativity theorems, spectral convergence lemmas, and Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) optimality conditions, see Supplementary Material S1 (Mathematical Appendix).

Within the framework of Gaussian Markov Random Fields (GGM; Lauritzen, 1996; Whittaker, 1990), the precision matrix 𝐊 = (𝑘 𝑖𝑗 ) is defined as the direct inverse of the correlation matrix: where the off-diagonal elements 𝑘 𝑖𝑗 represent unstandardized concentration coefficients.

text.text: >Study 2: Multi-Sample and Multi-Instrument Empirical Validation
text.formatted: <head n="4." >Study 2: Multi-Sample and Multi-Instrument Empirical Validation</head>

text.text: To evaluate the empirical applicability, cross-sample validity, and diagnostic capacity of rEGA in real-world data, we conducted a secondary analysis across three independent, screened samples totaling 𝑁 = 3,200 Colombian adult participants.

The databases were drawn exclusively from the open-science repository of Ruiz et al. (2024), collected via non-probabilistic sampling under ethical protocols approved by the institutional review board of the Fundación Universitaria Konrad Lorenz (Bogotá, Colombia), with prior informed consent obtained across three distinct cohorts: Sample 1 (Community; 𝑁 = 2,398 in AAQ-II / 2,393 in DASS-21; 62.4% women; age 𝑀 = 28.6 years, 𝑆𝐷 = 9.4, range = 18--68; 63.8% undergraduate/college graduates, 18.4% postgraduate, and 17.8% secondary education); Sample 2 (Clinical; 𝑁 = 358; 68.2% women; age 𝑀 = 34.1 years, 𝑆𝐷 = 11.2, range = 18--65); and Sample 3 (General; 𝑁 = 444 in AAQ-II only; 66.7% women; age 𝑀 = 27.6 years, 𝑆𝐷 = 9.6, range = 18--62; 61.3% secondary/technical education, 25.9% undergraduate, and 12.8% postgraduate).

Two widely used self-report psychometric instruments were evaluated: First, the Acceptance and Action Questionnaire-II (AAQ-II; Bond et al., 2011) was administered using the Spanish adaptation validated for Latin America by Ruiz et al. (2016).

(2016)</ref>.

text.text: The AAQ-II comprises 7 items (operationally labeled PI1 to PI7).
Items are rated on a 7-point Likert-type scale ranging from 1 (never true) to 7 (always true), where higher scores reflect greater psychological inflexibility.

Although the AAQ-II was designed as a unidimensional measure of Psychological Inflexibility, it has been the subject of ongoing debate regarding its items' putative lack of discriminant validity against affective distress (Ruiz et al., 2024; Wolgast, 2014) and its pronounced vulnerability to artificial over-fragmentation induced by lexical local dependence between redundant item pairs (e.g., items 1-4 and 2-3; Ruiz et al., 2016).

text.text: This property makes the AAQ-II an ideal case study for evaluating across all samples rEGA's capacity to diagnose lexical doublets and preserve the global unidimensionality of the test (Phase 2A).
Second, the Depression, Anxiety, and Stress Scales-21 (DASS-21; Lovibond & Lovibond, 1995) was evaluated using the Spanish version validated for Hispanic populations by Daza et al. (2002).

(2002)</ref>.

text.text: The DASS-21 is a 21-item tripartite scale organized into three latent dimensions of 7 items each: Depression (D1 to D7; e.g., anhedonia and lack of meaning), Anxiety (A1 to A7; e.g., physiological hyperarousal and subjective anxious experience), and Stress (S1 to S7; e.g., tension and irritability).
Items are rated on a 4-point Likert scale assessing symptom frequency over the past week, from 0 (did not apply to me at all) to 3 (applied to me very much, or most of the time).

The structure of the DASS-21 is notable in psychometric network research (Isvoranu & Epskamp, 2023) for featuring transdiagnostic bridge symptoms alongside peripheral somatic indicators (e.g., A1 "dryness of mouth").

text.text: Across all 972 evaluated experimental conditions (Table 1; Figure 1), rEGA-Leiden demonstrated superior accuracy in recovering the population dimensional structure, achieving an overall Percentage of Correct Classification of 87.65% (𝑀 = .877, 𝑀𝑑𝑛 = 1.000, 𝑆𝐷 = .229) and a Mean Absolute Error of MAE = .128 (𝑀𝑑𝑛 = .000).
text.formatted: Across all 972 evaluated experimental conditions (Table <ref type="table">1</ref>; Figure <ref type="figure">1</ref>), rEGA-Leiden demonstrated superior accuracy in recovering the population dimensional structure, achieving an overall Percentage of Correct Classification of 87.65% (𝑀 = .877, 𝑀𝑑𝑛 = 1.000, 𝑆𝐷 = .229) and a Mean Absolute Error of MAE = .128 (𝑀𝑑𝑛 = .000).

text.text: By contrast, conventional EGA based on Walktrap obtained an overall accuracy rate of 64.81% (MAE = .512), EGA with Louvain reached 69.77% (MAE = .421), and traditional Parallel Analysis (PA-PCA) achieved 71.32% (MAE = .389).

Moreover, whereas Walktrap and Louvain exhibited a systematic tendency toward over-factoring (MBE = +.793 and MBE = +.681, respectively), rEGA-Leiden reduced classification bias to near-zero levels (MBE = +.075, 𝑀𝑑𝑛 = .000) while attaining a higher Adjusted Rand Index (ARI = .800, 𝑀𝑑𝑛 = .950).
Under the regime of contamination by bridging variance and noisy items (P1 Bridge Noise; Table 1), methods relying on unweighted adjacency matrices showed pronounced vulnerability.

text.text: In unidimensional structures (𝐾 = 1) with weak factor loadings (𝜆 = .400), EGA-Walktrap and EGA-Louvain collapsed to accuracy rates of 15.00% to 21.80% and 6.70% to 8.90%, respectively.
Conversely, the topological purity-weighted adjacency matrix (𝐀 rEGA ) protected the graph structure, enabling rEGA-Leiden to sustain accuracy rates between 81.70% and 89.00% within this regime.

In the presence of local dependence driven by lexical doublets (P2 Local Dependence), rEGA-Leiden maintained accuracy rates between 70.80% and 91.90% across all levels of local dependence, whereas Walktrap and Louvain dropped to ranges of 17.30% to 32.50%.
Finally, comparisons across response formats confirmed the metric equivalence of rEGA-Leiden in continuous Gaussian data (84.90% accuracy in P0) and ordinal polytomous data (87.10% in P0).

text.text: The present study introduced, algebraically formalized, and validated Reliability Exploratory Graph Analysis (rEGA), an analytical framework designed to integrate conditional measurement error decomposition and metric reliability estimation within Exploratory Graph Analysis.

Although network psychometrics has established a conceptually sound alternative to common-cause models through Gaussian Markov Random Fields (GGM; Borsboom et al., 2021; Epskamp et al., 2017 Epskamp et al., , 2018b;; Schmittmann et al., 2011) and the EGA paradigm has shown notable effectiveness in dimensionality identification (Christensen et al., 2023b; Golino & Epskamp, 2017; Golino et al., 2020a Golino et al., , 2020b)), existing workflows operated on the partial correlation matrix while discarding the conditional precision diagonal.

On the one hand, in transdiagnostic bridge nodescharacterized by high Global Topological Purity (ℎ 𝒢,𝑖2 = ℎ 𝑖 2 + 𝛽 𝑖 2 ) driven predominantly by bridging variance (𝛽 𝑖 2 ), as seen in items D2, S3, and S6 of the DASS-21-oscillation between adjacent clusters in clinical samples reflects genuine comorbidity across syndromes (Borsboom et al., 2021).

text.text: Whereas topological reduction procedures such as Unique Variable Analysis (UVA; Christensen et al., 2023a) suggest combining locally dependent variables into reduced composite scores, merging a noisy item with other nodes in the presence of high Markov uniqueness is counterproductive because it injects and propagates error variance (𝜓 𝑖 2 ) into the combined indicator.

Instead, rEGA automatically quantifies and attenuates such excess noise in the matrix 𝐴 𝑖𝑗 rEGA and in the computation of SEM 𝑡 raw , preserving the integrity of the canonical scale without resorting to manual pruning or arbitrary cutoffs.

text.text: In the first stage, corresponding to graph estimation and sample support, the researcher fits the model using the function rEGA(data, algorithm = "leiden", gamma = 0.50, seed = 11) on polychoric or Pearson correlation matrices (cor_auto).

Because the accuracy of restricted maximum likelihood refitting (𝐊 ̂refit ) and the recovery of Markov conditional uniqueness (𝜓 𝑖 2 ) follow an error reduction rate of order 𝒪(1/√𝑁), maximizing sample size is recommended in high-dimensional networks or clinical samples with elevated comorbidity to narrow the variability of the resolvent operator and ensure community detection stability.

In the second stage, focused on structural evaluation via the Nodal Dominance Rule, the compositional decomposition ℎ 𝑖 2 + 𝛽 𝑖 2 + 𝜓 𝑖 2 ≡ 1.000 should be inspected before accepting the graph partition.

If the algorithm delineates multiple communities but the Nodal Triad reveals systematic variance leakage (𝛽 ̅ 2 > ℎ ̅ 2 ), the leakage ratio (𝛽 ̅ 2 /ℎ ̅ 2 > 1.000) proves that the subdivision is an artifact induced by modularity optimization in the presence of lexical local dependence, indicating that the unidimensional structure or canonical theoretical architecture should be retained.

text.text: In the third stage, addressing the functional audit of indicators without resorting to ad hoc test truncation, items are classified according to the relative dominance of their components into: (a) core items, defined by the dominance of within-factor communality over bridging variance (ℎ 𝑖 2 > 𝛽 𝑖 2 ) and low Markov uniqueness, acting as pure dimension markers; (b) transdiagnostic bridge nodes, characterized by bridging variance comparable to or exceeding within-factor communality (𝛽 𝑖2 ≥ ℎ 𝑖 2 ) alongside high global topological purity (ℎ 𝒢,𝑖2 = 1 -𝜓 𝑖 2 ), which should be retained within their canonical theoretical dimensions without removal even if they exhibit bootstrap assignment instability; and (c) noisy or defective items, identified by the dominance of Markov conditional uniqueness (𝜓 𝑖 2 > ℎ 𝒢,𝑖 2 ), whose conditional error is attenuated by the adjacency matrix 𝐴 𝑖𝑗 rEGA and documented for future content revisions of the instrument.

text.text: In the fourth stage, concerning the metric reporting of reliability, measurement error, and bootstrap inference, the function boot.rEGA(rEGA.obj = fit, iter = 500, type = "resampling", seed = 11) is executed to derive point estimates and 95% confidence intervals for Γ 𝑐 , Γ 𝑡 , Ψ 𝒢 , and SEM raw , accompanied by the observed standard deviation (𝑆 𝑌 ) of composite scores in the analyzed sample.

Rather than applying rigid universal cutoffs from Classical Test Theory, researchers should interpret Within-Community Coefficient Gamma (Γ 𝑐 ) as the isolated specific precision of the syndrome within its conditioned subgraph 𝐐 𝑐 (the topologically purified network analogue of subscale 𝜔 𝑠 , immune to the comorbidity-induced collapse of bifactor 𝜔 ℎ𝑠 ; see Theorem 4 in Supplementary Material S1), Total Coefficient Gamma (Γ 𝑡 ) as the precision of global systemic severity, and use the Standard Error of Measurement of the Graph (SEM 𝑡 raw ) to construct individual confidence intervals and disattenuate relationships with external variables, in strict compliance with the REGEMA guidelines (Sánchez-Meca et al., 2021) and the AERA, APA, and NCME (2014) Standards.

text.text: The scope of the present study is subject to methodological boundaries that outline priority avenues for the research agenda in network psychometrics.

First, the current formulation of the resolvent operator is framed within Gaussian Graphical Models (GGMs) for continuous and ordered polytomous data; generalizing the nodal variance framework to discontinuous or non-Gaussian structures, such as Ising binary networks and Mixed Graphical Models (MGMs; Haslbeck & Waldorp, 2020), represents a natural extension of the model.

text.text: Third, the interaction between nodal topological purity and community detection algorithms opens opportunities to examine optimization functions tailored to psychometric topology by isolating hybrid combinations to deepen these findings, as well as to link the rEGA reliability framework with complementary local dependence methodologies (Christensen et al., 2023a), structural invariance tests (Jamison et al., 2024), and longitudinal models (Christensen & Golino, 2021).

text.text: Finally, because rEGA evaluates a closed compositional system sensitive to graph density, we refrained from setting universal static cutoffs; future research may further investigate the dynamic calibration of decision thresholds as a function of network structural characteristics (Burger et al., 2023; Elson et al., 2023).

Notwithstanding these considerations, rEGA bridges the longstanding divide between conditional graph topology and psychometric measurement precision theory.

By recovering the debiased precision diagonal via 𝐊 ̂refit , formulating the Law of Conservation of the Nodal Triad (ℎ 𝑖 2 + 𝛽 𝑖 2 + 𝜓 𝑖 2 ≡ 1.000), and deriving the Gamma Coefficients (Γ 𝑐 , Γ 𝑡 ) alongside the Standard Error of Measurement of the Graph (SEM 𝑡 raw ), this framework provides an exact analytical solution for decoupling internal structure validation from score error estimation.

In doing so, rEGA preserves the integrity of canonical psychological scales against ad hoc modifications, securing individual error metrics and ensuring strict compliance with REGEMA guidelines and international measurement standards.
